data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The cuts create a maximum of 8 regions because 4 lines concurrent at a point yield exactly 2n regions, as the intersection multiplicity at the origin restricts the plane division.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the lines are perturbed slightly to avoid the central point, they would intersect each other pairwise, increasing the number of regions towards 11.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If zero-width lines are treated as non-dividers, the entire pizza remains 1 piece.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The general maximum number of regions R formed by n lines in a plane is R = (n^2 + n + 2)/2. For n=4, this yields 11. However, this maximum assumes no three lines intersect at a single point. By forcing all 4 lines to pass through the center, we introduce triple and quadruple intersections. Each time three lines meet at a single point instead of three distinct pairwise points, the number of regions decreases by 1. With 4 lines meeting at one point, we lose regions compared to the 11-piece maximum. The absolute minimum configuration for n lines is all concurrent, yielding exactly 2n = 8 regions.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
